pts.guide: Critical distinction: training happens offline (can take hours), inference happens at runtime (must be fast). This shapes all optimization decisions. You don't need to run training, but understand why it's separate.
pts.text: Training and inference are fundamentally different operations with different computational and latency requirements.

pts.guide: Need intuition: gradients show which direction improves the model, weights are adjusted to reduce error. The math is optional; understanding that it's iterative and can get stuck locally is essential.
pts.text: Backpropagation is the algorithm that allows neural networks to learn by calculating gradients and updating weights.

pts.guide: Recognize overfitting in your metrics (training accuracy way higher than validation). Causes: too much capacity, too little data, too many epochs. Fixes: regularization, more data, early stopping. Skip mathematical proofs.
pts.text: Overfitting occurs when a model memorizes training data rather than learning generalizable patterns.

pts.guide: This is often overlooked but critical: spending engineering time on a bad dataset is wasted. Understand data pipelines, validation, labeling quality. You'll spend more time here than on novel architectures.
pts.text: Dataset quality directly determines model quality; bad data produces bad models regardless of architecture.

pts.guide: Basic rule: never train on test data. Understand train/val/test splits and why data leakage kills results. Cross-validation is nice-to-know but not essential for PMs.
pts.text: Validation splits and test sets are essential for measuring actual model performance without overfitting to metrics.

pts.guide: Key insight: filters slide across images finding features (edges, textures, shapes). Why this matters for digital humans: face detection, synthesis, expression recognition. Understand "why convolution beats fully-connected layers for images"—don't memorize architecture details.
pts.text: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) use local feature detection (filters) to efficiently process images.

pts.guide: Critical for lip-sync and body animation. Understand the vanishing gradient problem (why plain RNNs fail) and that LSTMs solve it with gates. Don't memorize LSTM equations; know that they remember long-term dependencies better.
pts.text: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and LSTMs process sequential data by maintaining hidden state across time steps.

pts.guide: High-level: attention weights say "which parts of input matter for this output." This is why transformers beat RNNs. You need to understand the concept, not compute attention matrices.
pts.text: Attention mechanisms allow models to focus on relevant parts of input, improving performance on long sequences.

pts.guide: This is the foundation of LLMs and modern generative models. Know: parallel processing (faster than RNNs), scales better, why it enabled large models. Skip positional encodings and multi-head math.
pts.text: Transformer architecture uses self-attention to process all tokens in parallel, enabling massive scale and better parallelization.

pts.guide: Understand: tokenization (text → numbers), context window limits, why fine-tuning works. This directly impacts any text-to-speech or description features in your product. Know the cost/latency tradeoffs.
pts.text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are transformer-based models trained on massive text corpora to predict next tokens.

pts.guide: Why it matters: you won't train models from scratch. Fine-tuning on creator data, scripts, or brand guidelines is practical. Understand it's cheaper and faster than training from zero; comes with data contamination risks.
pts.text: Fine-tuning adapts pre-trained models to specific tasks with relatively small amounts of task-specific data.

pts.guide: This powers modern image and video synthesis. Conceptually: start with noise, gradually denoise to generate output. Why this matters: face synthesis, video generation quality depends on this. Understand sampling/inference is expensive; training is even more so.
pts.text: Diffusion models generate images/video by iteratively denoising random noise, learning to reverse a corruption process.

pts.guide: Historically important for face synthesis. Modern diffusion models often replace GANs now. Know the concept: generator makes fake data, discriminator judges it, both improve. Training is notoriously unstable; understand mode collapse.
pts.text: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) use competition between generator and discriminator networks to produce realistic outputs.

pts.guide: Understand: synthetic faces must look real (perceptual quality), preserve identity (consistency), handle diverse ethnicities (bias issues). Know that synthetic faces can have artifacts at certain angles/lighting.
pts.text: Face synthesis creates realistic facial appearances by learning from datasets; requires quality training data and handles identity preservation.

pts.guide: This is a latency-sensitive problem: misaligned lips destroy believability instantly. Understand: requires audio analysis, mouth shape prediction, and sometimes keyframe adjustment. Latency requirements are strict (sub-100ms desirable).
pts.text: Lip-sync alignment maps audio to mouth movements, solving the audio-visual synchronization problem in digital humans.

pts.guide: Understand quality spectrum: concatenative (older, robotic) to neural (current, natural). Inference is relatively fast. Emotions, voice cloning, language support vary by provider. Know latency is usually acceptable for most creator use cases.
pts.text: Text-to-Speech (TTS) converts written text to natural-sounding audio with controllable emotion, accent, and prosody.

pts.guide: Less critical than face/lip-sync for current products but growing. Understand: limited motion capture data causes artifacts, real-time rendering requires optimization. Full-body synthesis is harder than facial.
pts.text: Body animation and motion synthesis generate realistic body movement from pose estimates or motion capture data.

pts.guide: Strategic decision for product roadmap. 2D: stream videos, works on any device, limited control. 3D: full control, interactive, but requires powerful clients or streaming. Understand latency and bandwidth implications of each.
pts.text: 2D vs 3D rendering tradeoff: 2D video synthesis is faster/cheaper but less flexible; 3D avatars enable real-time interaction but require more compute.

pts.guide: This is where problems hide. Understand: data sources, validation checks, handling missing/corrupt data, ensuring no data leakage. You'll spend more time here than on novel ML. Automation reduces human error.
pts.text: Data pipelines extract, clean, validate, and prepare data for training; quality directly impacts model performance.

pts.guide: Know: models need to be versioned, metrics tracked across experiments, best checkpoints saved. Tools like MLflow/Weights&Biases. Reproducibility matters for debugging failures and comparing variants.
pts.text: Training pipelines orchestrate model training with logging, checkpointing, and experiment tracking for reproducibility.

pts.guide: Critical for creators: how do we serve inference to millions? Batching (higher throughput), caching (lower latency), GPU pooling. Understand serving is often the bottleneck, not model training.
pts.text: Model serving infrastructure deploys trained models to production with requirements for latency, throughput, and cost efficiency.

pts.guide: Quantization: lower precision (int8 instead of float32), speeds up inference. Pruning: remove unimportant weights. Distillation: train smaller model to mimic large one. Caching: reuse recent results. All have quality/speed tradeoffs.
pts.text: Inference optimization techniques (quantization, pruning, distillation, caching) reduce latency and cost while maintaining quality.

pts.guide: Offline metrics (accuracy, BLEU, etc.) don't always match user experience. A/B tests measure real impact. For generative models, need human evaluation or proxy metrics. Understand statistical significance and minimum detectable effect.
pts.text: A/B testing and evaluation frameworks measure model quality in production, not just offline metrics.

pts.guide: Models degrade over time (data distribution shifts, new edge cases, user behavior changes). Need automated alerts for quality drops. This catches problems before creators complain. Essential for maintaining trust.
pts.text: Monitoring and observability track model performance drift, data drift, and system health in production.

pts.guide: For real-time digital humans, latency kills UX. But optimizations (quantization, pruning) can degrade quality. Your roadmap must balance: fast but meh vs slow but beautiful. Understand which features are latency-sensitive (lip-sync: yes; video rendering: maybe).
pts.text: Latency vs quality tradeoff: lower latency requires inference optimization which may reduce output quality; product decisions must balance both.

pts.guide: This directly impacts creator economics. If inference costs $0.10/video and creators earn $5 per video, margins disappear. Optimization (distillation, quantization) reduces cost. Batching amortizes fixed costs. Pricing must account for ML cost.
pts.text: Cost per inference scales with model size and compute; larger models are slower and more expensive unless optimized.

pts.guide: For most features, don't train from scratch. Use pre-trained models, fine-tune on your data. Exception: core differentiator features where you need custom advantage. Face synthesis might be build; TTS might be buy (e.g., Azure, Google).
pts.text: Build vs buy decisions for ML: home-grown models give control but require expertise; off-the-shelf solutions are faster but less differentiated.
